servers.name: Gigwa MCP
servers.attribution: Anestis Gkanogiannis and contributors
servers.installation: Install gigwa-mcp separately into a Python >=3.10 environment; configure GIGWA_URL and optional paired GIGWA_USER/GIGWA_PASS.
servers.effects: Tools may upload data, modify Gigwa, or write local result files; inspect each tool before invocation.

servers.name: Chorus
servers.attribution: Dmitry Penzar, Lorenzo Ruggeri, Rosalba Giugno, Luca Pinello and contributors
servers.installation: Install the pinellolab/chorus source project and provision its oracle environments, model weights and references separately. The PyPI package named chorus is unrelated. Set executable_path to the installed chorus-mcp.
servers.effects: Predictions can consume GPU/CPU, write reports, and download missing model assets inside the upstream server. Pre-provision assets when offline.

servers.name: MaveDB-Link
servers.attribution: Bernt Popp and mavedb-link contributors
servers.installation: For stdio, install the source project's dependencies in Python >=3.12 and set workdir to that checkout and executable_path to its Python. The author-documented HTTP service is available with transport='http'.
servers.effects: Reads local MaveDB mirrors or contacts the MaveDB API; HTTP mode sends tool arguments to the author's hosted service.

servers.name: BioMCP
servers.attribution: Ian Maurer, GenomOncology and contributors
servers.installation: Install genomoncology/biomcp separately; its PyPI distribution is biomcp-cli, not the unrelated biomcp distribution. The installed executable is biomcp.
servers.effects: Contacts upstream biomedical APIs according to the selected tool; some sources require credentials.

servers.name: Juicebox MCP
servers.attribution: Jim Robinson, Douglass Turner and contributors
servers.installation: Prepare the official source checkout and npm dependencies separately, then set workdir to the checkout and executable_path to Node if necessary.
servers.effects: Starts the MCP server and local browser communication service; visualization tools may require an attached Juicebox frontend and network datasets.

servers.name: GeneChat MCP
servers.attribution: Nate Costello and GeneChat contributors
servers.installation: Install and initialize GeneChat and its local genome/annotation databases separately. GENECHAT_CONFIG optionally selects an existing TOML configuration.
servers.effects: Reads configured local genomes; returned tool results can include individual genotypes.

servers.name: GenePattern MCP
servers.attribution: GenePattern team and contributors; underlying platform: Reich et al., GenePattern 2.0 (2006)
servers.installation: Install the official source checkout requirements separately with Python >=3.11. Set workdir to the checkout, executable_path to that Python, and GENEPATTERN_KEY to an existing API token.
servers.effects: Selected tools can submit GenePattern jobs, upload data, or download files. Uses GenePattern cloud by default or the explicitly configured GENEPATTERN_URL.

servers.name: BrAPI MCP
servers.attribution: Casey Hand (cyanheads) and contributors; community BrAPI implementation
servers.installation: Separately prepare the pinned @cyanheads/brapi-mcp-server release/source with its dist build and dependencies; set workdir to the package root and executable_path to Node >=24. The bridge never runs npm, npx, bunx or an installer.
servers.effects: Queries BrAPI servers; opt-in upstream tools can submit observations or export local data. Connection aliases and dataframes require call_mcp_workflow to preserve a session.
limitations: Interface integration does not implement genomic selection or validate breeding predictions.

servers.name: Ensembl MCP (cyanheads)
servers.attribution: Casey Hand (cyanheads) and contributors; community wrapper, not an Ensembl-authored server
servers.installation: Separately prepare the pinned @cyanheads/ensembl-mcp-server build and dependencies; set workdir to the package root and executable_path to Node >=24.
servers.effects: Sends selected gene, sequence, variant and homology queries to Ensembl REST or the configured mirror.

servers.name: BioThings MCP
servers.attribution: Anton Kulaga and Longevity Genie contributors
servers.installation: Install the pinned longevity-genie/biothings-mcp project separately in Python >=3.10; use its installed biothings-mcp entry point.
servers.effects: Queries BioThings services and may write cached/exported result data under the upstream output directory.

servers.name: gget MCP
servers.attribution: Anton Kulaga, Newton Winter and Longevity Genie contributors; gget method authors retain their own credit
servers.installation: Install gget-mcp and its separately specified gget dependencies in Python >=3.10; the verified command is gget-mcp stdio.
servers.effects: Queries gget-supported services; selected tools may run external searches, load models, download assets or write outputs.
limitations: Individual tools and their dependencies require separate validation; tool count is not an independent-algorithm count.

servers.name: UCSC Genome MCP
servers.attribution: Henry Lydecker (hlydecker) and contributors; community UCSC wrapper
servers.installation: Prepare the pinned source checkout and its requirements in Python >=3.10, set workdir to the checkout and executable_path to that Python. Use the existing hyphenated ucsc-genome-mcp.py script; upstream README/packaging also mention nonexistent underscore filenames.
servers.effects: Sends genome, track, region and sequence queries to UCSC and caller-selected public assembly hubs.
limitations: The pinned upstream script sometimes encodes application errors as ordinary text. DNAKit recognizes its verified error prefixes and preserves the original flag as upstream_isError when normalizing them. Other tool-specific content still needs inspection.

servers.name: Open Targets MCP
servers.attribution: Nick Ren and contributors; community Open Targets wrapper
servers.installation: Install nickzren/opentargets-mcp separately in Python >=3.10; set executable_path to its interpreter. Uses the verified Python module entry point with explicit stdio.
servers.effects: Queries Open Targets evidence; results are research evidence and do not establish treatment suitability.

servers.name: Plant Genomics MCP
servers.attribution: Jaret Arnold (musharna) and contributors; community integration
servers.installation: Install the pinned plant-genomics-mcp Python distribution and dependencies separately. The plant-genomics-mcp entry point selects stdio; no HTTP token is needed for this local transport.
servers.effects: Queries plant genomics services and may submit selected sequences to NCBI BLAST. Configure the named NCBI contact-email variable before BLAST use.
limitations: The advertised hosted Tailscale endpoint has a bearer-token gate; it is not configured as an anonymous DNAKit endpoint.

servers.name: BioContextAI Knowledgebase MCP
servers.attribution: Malte Kuehl and the BioContextAI authors/contributors listed in the upstream citation
servers.installation: Install biocontext_kb separately in Python >=3.12. DNAKit fixes MCP_ENVIRONMENT=DEVELOPMENT for the verified stdio entry point.
servers.effects: Queries the selected biomedical knowledge services. The public hosted endpoint is described by its authors as testing-only and subject to fair use.
limitations: Data-source licenses and access limitations are separate; Google Scholar and KEGG are local-only in the upstream project.

servers.name: GrEBI
servers.attribution: EMBL-EBI SPOT / EBISPOT GrEBI contributors
servers.installation: Select transport='http' for the author-documented development service. Local deployment is a separate Java/API plus graph-database and HPC data-pipeline task; no local startup recipe is claimed here.
servers.effects: Sends queries to the EMBL-EBI development knowledge-graph service.
limitations: Development endpoint, without a production availability guarantee; no graph database or pipeline has been deployed by DNAKit.

servers.name: EBI Tools MCP (QuentinCody)
servers.license: Not specified in repository snapshot; remote service only, no upstream code bundled
servers.attribution: QuentinCody and repository contributors; community implementation, not an EMBL-EBI release
servers.installation: Select transport='http' for the repository author's published Cloudflare Worker MCP service. No standalone Node stdio entry point is present; no mcp-remote/npx helper is required by DNAKit.
servers.effects: Selected tools can submit sequences to EMBL-EBI Job Dispatcher and retrieve job results through a community-hosted service.
limitations: No LICENSE/LICENCE file or package license declaration was verified. Hosted transport availability is separate from job/scientific validation.

servers.name: GWAS MCP (muslus)
servers.attribution: ZaEyAsa (upstream package/LICENSE attribution) and muslus repository contributors
servers.installation: Prepare the pinned muslus/gwas-mcp source and its dependencies in an isolated Python >=3.10 environment, then point executable_path at that interpreter. Avoid assuming that the separately published gwas-mcp distribution has identical code.
servers.effects: Queries genomic evidence services; selected QC/association tools may execute local analyses and write files.
limitations: Repository owner and package author differ; the exact pinned source is the verified implementation. Individual analysis results have not been validated by DNAKit.

servers.name: NCBI Database MCP (hpend2373)
servers.license: MIT declared in pyproject.toml; standalone license text not found
servers.attribution: hpend2373 and Bio-MCP Project contributors (pyproject attribution)
servers.installation: Prepare the pinned NCBI-Database-MCP checkout and its requirements, set workdir to the checkout and executable_path to its Python. Uses the README-supported standard MCP script rather than executing its shell installer/launcher.
servers.effects: Queries NCBI gene/sequence/GEO resources; selected results can contain supplied gene or region queries.
limitations: MIT is a project metadata declaration; no standalone LICENSE file was found at the pinned revision.

servers.name: PubMed MCP (cyanheads)
servers.attribution: Casey Hand (cyanheads) and contributors; community literature server
servers.installation: Prepare the pinned @cyanheads/pubmed-mcp-server build and dependencies separately, then set workdir to the package root and executable_path to Node >=24.
servers.effects: Sends biomedical literature queries to PubMed/PMC, Europe PMC and optional Unpaywall; document permissions remain with the original sources.
limitations: Literature infrastructure, not a DNA prediction algorithm.

servers.name: ENCODE Toolkit
servers.attribution: Dr. Alex M. Mawla and contributors
servers.installation: Install the Python encode-toolkit distribution separately and set executable_path to its interpreter. DNAKit invokes the verified Python module directly; it does not use the npm shim which can bootstrap uv/Python.
servers.effects: Queries ENCODE experiments and files; selected upstream tools may download data, create workflows or manage local credential state.
limitations: Zenodo records are software archives, not automatically peer-reviewed papers. This bridge does not redistribute ENCODE Toolkit code.

servers.name: ToolUniverse
servers.attribution: Shanghua Gao, Marinka Zitnik and ToolUniverse paper/project contributors
servers.installation: Install the pinned ToolUniverse distribution and required provider dependencies separately. Use the installed tooluniverse console script; unlike the README uvx --refresh example, this bridge does not refresh or install anything.
servers.effects: Starts the compact ToolUniverse MCP catalog. Selected tools may contact services, load models, execute programs or write files according to their provider definitions.
limitations: Cross-disciplinary aggregate: not every exposed tool is DNA-related, and tool counts are not independent-algorithm counts. Provider credentials/dependencies must be configured separately.

servers.name: AWS Kiro Life Sciences: genomics
servers.license: MIT-0 in root LICENSE.txt; MIT declared by component pyproject.toml
servers.attribution: Amazon.com, Inc. or its affiliates; Kiro Life Sciences Contributors
servers.installation: Prepare the pinned aws-samples/sample-kiro-power-life-sciences source. Separately install life-sciences-common and the life-sciences-genomics component in its Python >=3.10 environment, then set executable_path to the installed life-sciences-genomics console script. No uvx or automatic install is used.
servers.effects: Selected tools query external biological resources; molecular-analysis and workflow tools can submit sequences or access local result files. Named credentials are forwarded only for providers that need them.
limitations: Alpha sample component. Its entry point, tool definitions and stdio transport are source-verified; each underlying provider endpoint and scientific output still needs separate validation.
This component is part of one AWS Kiro project; it is not counted as an independent scientific algorithm.

All provider-client source files in this selected component were inspected for fixed/mock analysis paths. Providers and complete scientific outputs have not been independently validated; a successful MCP call is not evidence of valid biological analysis.

servers.name: PubMed (Anthropic Life Sciences hosted connector)
servers.license: Remote provider terms; the marketplace does not grant an independent server-code license
servers.attribution: U.S. National Library of Medicine (as attributed by the Anthropic marketplace); Anthropic marketplace maintainers
servers.installation: Select transport=http. The provider-published endpoint supports anonymous MCP initialization and tools/list as verified on 2026-09-20. No local installer is run.
capabilities: article metadata, full text and copyright status
servers.effects: Queries are sent to the named public biological/literature service. Returned articles and data retain provider-specific terms.
limitations: Only initialization and tools/list were exercised; provider query results and scientific conclusions were not validated.

servers.name: Open Targets Platform official MCP
servers.license: Remote provider terms; the marketplace does not grant an independent server-code license
servers.attribution: OpenTargets (as attributed by the Anthropic marketplace); Anthropic marketplace maintainers
servers.installation: Select transport=http. The provider-published endpoint supports anonymous MCP initialization and tools/list as verified on 2026-09-20. No local installer is run.
capabilities: live Open Targets GraphQL schema and queries
servers.effects: Queries are sent to the named public biological/literature service. Returned articles and data retain provider-specific terms.
limitations: Only initialization and tools/list were exercised; provider query results and scientific conclusions were not validated.

servers.name: 10x Genomics Cloud MCP
servers.license: MIT (MCP connector); separate 10x Cloud and TXG CLI terms apply
servers.attribution: 10x Genomics, Inc.
servers.installation: Separately prepare and unpack the upstream 10x Genomics MCP bundle, including its server/, node_modules/ and platform bin/ files. Set workdir to that unpacked bundle, executable_path to installed Node.js >=18, and the named TXG_CLI_ACCESS_TOKEN environment variable. DNAKit does not download a bundle or TXG binary.
capabilities: Cell Ranger and ATAC analysis submission and monitoring
servers.effects: Selected tools can upload sequencing files, read or modify cloud projects and references, and start paid analyses. Upstream only sets accept-payment=true when that tool argument is explicitly supplied.
limitations: Source and manifest entry points are verified. No 10x account, access token, TXG binary, cloud job or scientific result was exercised. This is one component of the Anthropic marketplace entry.
